lesson.title: Read the protractor
lesson.subtitle: P4 angle revision
lesson.objective: Choose the right scale and read an angle in degrees.
lesson.story: An angle is drawn on a protractor.

steps.title: Choose the scale
steps.prompt: The base arm of this angle lies along the right end of the baseline. Which scale should you read?
hints: Find the 0 on each scale. One 0 is at the right end and the other is at the left end.
Read the scale whose 0 is on the same end as the base arm.
The base arm is on the right, so use the scale that starts with 0 on the right.

steps.title: Read the angle
steps.prompt: What is the size of the angle in degrees? Enter the number.
hints: Read where the second arm crosses the scale that starts at 0 on the base arm.
Long marks are every 10 degrees and short marks are every 5 degrees. Count along from 0.
The arm crosses just after 70, exactly on that long mark.

steps.title: Name the angle
steps.prompt: Is the angle acute, a right angle or obtuse?
hints: Compare with a right angle, which is exactly 90 degrees.
Is your reading smaller than 90, equal to 90, or larger than 90?
The angle is 70°, which is less than 90°.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why must you start reading from the 0 on the base arm?

choices.label: Both scales count the same turn, so either one gives the right size.
The angle is always the bigger of the two numbers printed on the scales.
The angle opens from its base arm, so the count must start at 0 there.

hints: Think about where the angle starts.
An angle is measured from one arm to the other.
The two scales give different numbers for the same arm.
Choose the explanation about starting from 0 on the base arm.
